'''Hans-Peter Hauri''' (born 13 February 1945 in Zürich) is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[biologist]]<ref>[https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/emeriti-former-professors/emeriti/hans-peter-hauri Prof. Dr. Hans-Peter Hauri, Emeritus]. biozentrum.unibas.ch. Retrieved 2023-11-08</ref>

== Life ==
{{BLP sources section|date=November 2023}}
Hans-Peter Hauri, [[Emeritus|Professor emeritus]] of [[OMICS Publishing Group|Cell Biology]], conducted research at the [[Biozentrum University of Basel|Biozentrum]] of the [[University of Basel]] from 1983 to 2010. After completing biology studies at the [[University of Zurich]] followed by a doctoral thesis in 1973, he joined the Pediatric Clinic at the [[Inselspital|University Hospital of Bern]]. In 1978 he moved as a postdoc to the [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] and [[Harvard University]], in [[Boston]]. In 1980 he returned to Switzerland and began research in [[Urs A. Meyer]]‘s Group, initially at the University of Zurich and later at the Biozentrum. Here he was appointed Associate Professor and in 2004 Professor of Cell Biology. In addition, he served as Director of Studies in Biology and Dean of the Faculty of Science at the University of Basel.

Hauri completed his doctoral dissertation, ''Ein invasives Neoplasma aus embryonalen Zellen von Drosophila melanogaster in Dauerkultur in vivo'', at the University of Zürich in 1974.<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Hauri|first=Hans-Peter|title=Ein invasives Neoplasma aus embryonalen Zellen von Drosophila melanogaster in Dauerkultur in vivo|year=1974|url=https://archive.org/details/IA41507208_0060|type=Doctoral thesis}}</ref>

== Work ==
Hans-Peter Hauri studied protein [[secretion]], involving the movement of these proteins from the site of synthesis to their intended destination, during which the integrity of the cell organelles remained preserved.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =17965257 | volume=35 | issue=5 | pages= 970–3| title=Visualization of protein interactions inside the secretory pathway | date=2007-11-01 | journal=Biochem Soc Trans | last1=Nyfeler | first1=B | last2=Hauri | first2=H-P | doi=10.1530/REP-07-0249 }}</ref> Hauri discovered that the [[membrane protein]] CLIMP-63 mediates the interaction of the [[endoplasmic reticulum]] (ER) and [[microtubule]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =16683914| volume=7 | issue=6| pages= 3507–14| title=Morphogenesis of the endoplasmic reticulum: beyond active membrane expansion | date=2006-06-07 | journal=Traffic | last1=Vedrenne | first1=Cécile | last2=Hauri | first2=Hans-Peter | doi=10.1111/j.1600-0854.2006.00419.x }}</ref> In addition, he successfully established the ER-Golgi-intermediate compartment (ERGIC) as a cell organelle of the secretory pathway and could show that secretory proteins, produced in the ER, reach the [[Golgi apparatus|Golgi]] apparatus via [[ERGIC]].<ref>{{cite journal | pmid =16723730 | volume=119 | issue=1 | pages=2173–83| title=The ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC): in search of its identity and function | date=2006-06-01 | journal=J. Cell Sci. | last1=Appenzeller-Herzog | first1=Christian | last2=Hauri | first2=Hans-Peter| doi=10.1242/jcs.03019 }}</ref> Using a screening method, which he developed, he succeeded to systematically record protein interactions in the secretory pathway in living cells. Furthermore, he also elucidated the signaling networks of the secretory process.
